summary: A second-person horror episode: "you" wake up trapped somewhere that has gone wrong, a cryptic stranger hands over three numbered survival rules, and the story then tests each rule as the danger closes in. It ends on a cliffhanger with two options, and viewers vote in the comments to decide what happens in the next part.

beats.pattern: Narration speaks to the viewer as 'you': the hero dozes off in a familiar place and wakes to find it eerily empty. A persistent HUD (episode/location label, a clock that ticks forward, a passenger counter) plus a big 'PART 1' title card frame it like a game. A punch-in on the hero's wide eyes as he wakes; captions appear word by word with key words highlighted.

Uncanny detail: identical objects (glowing, ringing phones) sit on every seat. Close-up of one phone UI showing a missed-call count from a familiar contact, with vibration arcs and ringing SFX. Narration adds 'every seat... except one' as a teaser.

Reveal a silhouetted stranger sitting directly opposite and much too close (over-the-shoulder shot, glowing eyes). The silhouette resolves into a stern old helper in close-up, and the passenger counter ticks up by 1. His first spoken line is a warning not to touch the objects.
The hero checks his own phone and learns he is already far past his exit. An intercom/speaker graphic delivers the stakes: there is no way out. Clock HUD advances one minute.

The helper holds up a ticket/card. Handwritten list of 3 numbered rules fills the screen, then each rule pops up as a 'SURVIVAL RULE #N' card over reaction close-ups. Each rule is clearly set up to be tested later.

Two-shot of the pair facing each other, then the helper leans in. The hero snaps to a close-up as narration points out the helper knows something the hero never told him. The red caption word makes the helper's trustworthiness suddenly doubtful.

Rule 1 gets tested: lights go out section by section toward the hero (wide exterior tracking shot down a dark tunnel), until only the hero's seat stays lit. The scene shifts to red light: a tall grinning monster in uniform stands at the far end under a scrolling sign, and the counter ticks up again. A slow push-in on its face.

Rule 2 gets tested: the helper, dimmed and not turning around, whispers the rule in a red caption. The ringing stops, a phone picks up by itself (call timer UI with audio waveform), and a fake loved-one voice coaxes the hero to say his name. That tests rule 3.

The helper grabs the hero's wrist (two-shot). The destination sign scrolls a garbled name behind the monster's silhouette. The doors slide open onto total darkness, and the helper starts a final warning that gets cut off.
Jump-scare stinger: a gloved hand rests on the hero's shoulder from off-frame, then the monster's huge grinning face looms right behind the hero's head in a tight close-up.

'PART 2' card asks the viewer to choose. Two numbered callout labels point to parts of the scene (1 = go through the door, 2 = stay put). On-screen text says to comment 1 or 2 and that the most votes decide the next episode.

whyViral: The first line puts the viewer into the story as 'you' and opens on an instant mystery. A tense line or visual comes every 2-4 seconds. The game-like HUD (ticking clock, passenger counter that jumps when a new threat appears) works as a tension meter. The three numbered rules are a setup-and-payoff device: viewers memorize them, then watch each rule get tested, which makes them predict and pay attention. The helper's reliability gets flipped mid-story, which adds paranoia. The escalation is clear: empty → stranger → no exit → darkness closing in → monster → fake loved-one voice → the doors open. It ends on an unresolved jump scare and a binary vote (comment 1 or 2, most votes decide Part 2). That drives comments, gives viewers a say in the story, and brings them back for the next episode. Word-by-word captions with color-coded danger words keep the video watchable with the sound off. Rule cards and freeze-frame details give people a reason to rewatch.

cast.traits: ordinary young commuter in a hoodie, wide expressive eyes, silent, reacts in close-ups; stands in for the viewer
old, stern, calm, wears hat and scarf, gives the numbered rules, knows more than he should, so his trustworthiness is ambiguous
tall silhouette in uniform, glowing eyes, wide jagged grin, shown in red light, gets closer each time it appears
heard through a device, mimics a loved one, sweetly coaxes the hero to break a rule
